text: Should Resident contact the city housing inspector about the unit, Owner may decline to renew this Lease.
Tenant agrees that filing any complaint or lawsuit against Landlord is a default under this Lease, and Landlord may begin eviction proceedings.
Upon renewal, rent may be adjusted to the rate charged for comparable units in the community, with written notice as required by law.
Lessor shall have unrestricted access to the apartment at all hours for any purpose.
Resident consents to entry by Management, its employees, and contractors at any time and without advance notice.
Except in an emergency, Landlord will give notice before entering and will enter only between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m.
This Lease may not be terminated before the end of the term, and Tenant's receipt of military orders does not change this.
A service member may end this Lease only after 120 days' written notice and only if Landlord finds a replacement tenant.
A service member who receives permanent change of station orders may terminate this Lease by written notice and a copy of the orders, as provided in Va. Code § 55.1-1235.
Military Clause: Tenant may terminate upon receipt of PCS orders, provided Tenant pays a reletting fee equal to 85% of one month's rent.
Every early termination, whether for job relocation, military deployment, or any other reason, carries a $1,500 early termination charge.
A tenant who terminates under the military clause owes rent through the termination date and no early termination fee.
Tenant's personal circumstances, including obtaining a protective order, do not entitle Tenant to end this Lease early.
Tenant may terminate early only with 90 days' written notice and payment of all rent through the notice period, without exception.
A tenant who is a victim of family abuse and has a protective order may end this Lease with 28 days' written notice and a copy of the order.
A lease-break fee of two months' rent applies to any termination before the end of the term, with no exceptions.
If Resident terminates early for any reason, including a court protective order, Resident shall pay liquidated damages of $2,000.
No early termination fee applies when Tenant terminates under Va. Code § 55.1-1235 or § 55.1-1236.
If Tenant fails to pay rent when due, Landlord may deny Tenant access to the Premises until the balance is paid.
Owner may disconnect water and electric service to the unit after a notice of default goes unremedied for five days.
If Tenant does not pay rent, Landlord may give written notice and file an unlawful detainer action in general district court.
Resident shall pay a $35 trip charge each time maintenance staff respond to a work order.
A non-refundable annual repair fee of $200 is due at lease signing.
Tenant shall reimburse Landlord for the reasonable cost of repairing damage caused by Tenant, occupants, or guests.
Rent is payable only by credit card through RentPay, and a 3.5% service fee is added to each payment.
Landlord does not accept checks or money orders; each electronic payment is subject to a $7 processing charge.
Rent may be paid by check or money order at no charge, or online by card with the card processor's fee passed through at cost.
Landlord may modify any provision of this Lease, including the amount of rent, by mailing notice to Tenant 15 days in advance.
Tenant agrees to be bound by any amendment to this Lease that Owner posts on the resident portal.
This Lease may be amended only by a written document signed by both Landlord and Tenant.
Management may adopt new rules at any time, including rules that add monthly fees, and such rules bind Resident when emailed.
Community policies, as changed from time to time at Owner's sole discretion, are incorporated into this Lease and take effect immediately.
Landlord may adopt reasonable rules for the pool and parking areas after giving Tenant reasonable written notice.
Any rent increase for a renewal term will be communicated to Resident at least 21 days before the lease expires.
Owner may elect not to renew this Lease by giving Tenant 30 days' notice before the end of the term.
Tenant shall give Landlord 60 days' written notice of Tenant's intent to vacate at the end of the term.
For each day Tenant remains after the termination date, Tenant shall pay holdover rent equal to three times the daily rent.
Holding over will result in monthly rent of 250% of the current rent, due in full for any partial month.
If Tenant remains after the termination date in Landlord's notice, Tenant shall pay 125% of the daily rent for each day of holdover.
Upon Tenant's default, the entire balance of rent owed through the expiration of the term shall be accelerated and due at once.
Landlord shall be under no duty to relet the unit or otherwise mitigate damages after Tenant abandons it.
If Tenant vacates early, Tenant remains liable for rent until the unit is re-rented or the term ends, whichever comes first, and Landlord will make reasonable efforts to re-rent.
Rent shall not abate, and this Lease shall not terminate, if the dwelling is rendered uninhabitable by fire, flood, or other casualty.
In the event of fire damage, only Landlord may elect to terminate this Lease.
Tenant shall maintain renter's insurance covering Tenant's personal property against fire and theft.
Resident gives up any right to receive the notices described in the Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act before Owner files for possession.
By signing, Lessee releases every claim and remedy that state landlord-tenant law would otherwise provide, including the right to withhold rent into a court escrow.
Owner's acceptance of a partial rent payment does not waive Owner's right to collect the balance, and Resident keeps every right Resident has under Virginia law.
Lessee irrevocably names Lessor's counsel as Lessee's attorney-in-fact to admit liability and accept entry of a judgment for any sums claimed under this agreement.
Should Resident fall behind on rent, Resident agrees in advance that judgment may be entered against Resident for the amount Management certifies is due, with no hearing required.
Management may file suit in the general district court to collect unpaid rent, and Resident will be served and may appear to contest the claim.
Owner and its employees are released from all responsibility for personal injury or property loss in the apartment or common areas, even when caused by their own carelessness.
Resident will defend and reimburse Management for every claim, fine, or judgment arising from conditions in the unit, including those resulting from Management's failure to make repairs.
Resident is responsible for damage that Resident or Resident's guests cause through their own negligence; Owner remains responsible for harm caused by Owner's negligence.
Any legal expenses Management incurs in enforcing this agreement, including counsel fees for letters and phone calls, are charged to Resident's account as additional rent.
Lessee agrees to reimburse Lessor for all lawyer's fees in any dispute concerning the premises, even if Lessee wins.
Reasonable attorney fees may be awarded to the prevailing party only where the Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act allows such an award.
Resident shall pay to repair or replace the water heater, furnace, and any plumbing fixture that stops working, whatever the reason.
The unit is leased as-is. Owner makes no repairs to the electrical system, heating, or appliances during the term; Resident must arrange and pay for any such work.
Owner will keep the furnace, air conditioner, plumbing, wiring, and supplied appliances in good and safe working order, and Resident will report any problem promptly.
